Subject: BrightCart discovery — latency & throughput targets (post-call)

Hi Marissa / Karthik,

Thanks again for the call earlier — helpful to talk through how Redwood thinks about peak vs steady-state behavior and streaming. A quick recap from our side and the asks we promised to follow up on:

- Business context: BrightCart will use LLM inference for multi-turn checkout assistant + personalized recommendations. We expect bursty traffic around promos.
- Current expectation (internal): typical session = 6 interactions, median tokens/request ~900, occasional long prompts up to 6k tokens.
- Targeted client SLOs: 90th pct response time < 350ms for non-streaming completions; streaming latency for first token < 120ms.
- Procurement note: Finance asked for a rough committed capacity number to include in our vendor shortlist evaluation. They want a 30/60/90 day commitment estimate (very rough) to size a PO.

Can Redwood provide a short post-call note with:
1) a throughput hypothesis mapping: tokens/sec vs QPS vs concurrency for the workload we described (steady vs crest),
2) any immediate red flags on the streaming constraints we mentioned, and
3) what you need from our side before a sizing workshop.

I attached the call recording and our anonymized sample traffic CSV (columns: session_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, timestamp). I can also drop a Drive folder with raw session payloads if you need them.

Thanks — Ana

Ana — thanks for the clear recap and the sample CSV. Quick post-call hypotheses below (high level) to get the conversation started. We can turn these into a formal sizing workbook in the workshop.

Summary (top-line hypotheses)
- Steady-state baseline: ~25 QPS (concurrent sessions ~150), avg tokens/request = 900 => ~22.5k tokens/sec aggregate.
- Promotional crest (10–15 minute window): short bursts up to ~420 QPS (concurrency ~2.5k multiplexed sessions), avg tokens/request shifts to 1,100 => ~462k tokens/sec aggregate during crest.
- Long-prompt tail: 1–2% of requests hit >3k tokens which will increase per-request latency and require higher memory per replica for KV caching.

Mapping notes
- QPS <-> tokens/sec conversion depends on avg tokens/request. We used your median 900 and a crest median 1,100 to produce the numbers above. If your CSV suggests a different median, we’ll update.
- For non-streaming completions we target p95 latency < 400ms on dedicated capacity (with optimized batching). Your 90th at 350ms is achievable but depends on permitted batching window — smaller batching windows increase cost.
- Streaming: first-token latency target of <120ms looks feasible if: (a) sessions are sticky to the same worker, (b) we limit initial KV loads < 2k tokens or use prefix caching. Otherwise cold KV warmups can push first-token >200ms.

Immediate asks / What we need from BrightCart
- A sample of payload size distribution (you included tokens_in/out which is great) but we also need session duration distribution and percent of streaming sessions that stay open > 30s.
- Clarify acceptable cost/latency tradeoffs (e.g., are you comfortable with slightly higher p95 in exchange for 25% lower monthly spend?).
- Procurement: a rough committed capacity number (QPS or tokens/sec) you expect to consider for a 90-day PO will let us produce a simpler cost estimate.

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan)
1) Today: Redwood reviews the CSV and returns a filled sizing-hypothesis workbook (attached) with conservative / expected / aggressive scenarios. (Owner: Marissa)
2) Thu 6/12 — 60-minute sizing workshop: deep-dive on session shapes, streaming demo, joint assumptions. Tech leads: Karthik + Neha. (Owner: Ana / BrightCart to confirm)
3) Within 48 hours post-workshop: Redwood delivers a draft capacity commitment suggestion + cost range and a config checklist for streaming (how to pin sessions, caching knobs). (Owner: Marissa)

Attachment: sizing-hypothesis.xlsx (workbook with scenario tabs).

If that works, I’ll book Thu 6/12 10:00–11:00 PT. I added Karthik & Neha for the technical items you asked about.

Thanks — Marissa

Ana — quick technical clarifications ahead of the workshop:

- Streaming concurrency model: do you multiplex multiple sessions per GPU worker (application-side) or do you expect session stickiness? If you multiplex aggressively we can multiplex requests onto fewer replicas but that increases tail latency variance.
- KV cache sizing: for the long-prompt tail we need to know the max context tokens you expect to keep in active session cache. If >4k tokens we recommend provisioning higher-memory instances or using quantized KV storage.
- Session durations: please include the % of sessions with >60s open time. Long-lived streaming sessions are the bigger cost driver (they occupy connection capacity even between tokens).

Example minimal data we need for compute-sizing: payload percentiles (p50/p90/p99) for tokens_in, tokens_out, and session_duration_sec. If you can add these to the Drive folder before Thu that will let us finalize the conservative/aggressive scenarios.

Thanks — Karthik
